CHIEF COMPLAINT: Routine follow-up for toenail fungus.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: Patient is a 68-year-old ambulatory male with a longstanding history of onychomycosis of bilateral great toenails, present for routine follow-up. He reports the nails have been discolored for several years but denies any pain, denies difficulty walking, and denies any redness, swelling, or drainage around the nails. He is able to walk his usual 2 miles daily without any foot discomfort and has no complaints referable to his feet other than the cosmetic appearance of the nails. No history of diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, or immunosuppression.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Hypertension, hyperlipidemia.

MEDICATIONS: Lisinopril, atorvastatin.

PHYSICAL EXAM:
Vitals stable.
Feet: Bilateral great toenails with yellow-brown discoloration, mild subungual debris, and moderate thickening of the nail plate consistent with onychomycosis. Mild onycholysis noted at the distal nail edge. No periungual erythema, no warmth, no purulent drainage. Skin surrounding nails intact, no maceration or fissuring. Sensation intact to light touch, pulses 2+ bilaterally. Gait normal, no limping or altered weight-bearing observed. Patient ambulates independently without assistive device.

ASSESSMENT: Onychomycosis of bilateral great toenails, clinically evident by discoloration, thickening, and subungual debris. Patient remains asymptomatic from a functional standpoint - no pain, no gait disturbance, and no secondary infection identified.

PLAN: Discussed topical antifungal therapy (ciclopirox lacquer) as first-line treatment given absence of contraindication to antifungal use. Since the patient is not experiencing any limitation of ambulation, pain, or secondary infection related to the nail thickening, formal nail debridement is not indicated at this time on medical necessity grounds. Will continue to monitor; instructed patient to return if he develops pain, difficulty walking, or signs of infection around the nails. Follow-up in 6 months or sooner as needed.
